name: AI-Assisted SOC
description: Plays for a SOC where AI agents do the legwork and people approve, verify and own decisions. Steps start with "Agent:" or "Human:".

plays.title: Define agent scope and autonomy levels
plays.summary: Decide in writing what the agent may do alone, what needs a human approval, and what it must never do.
steps: Human: List agent actions in three tiers: autonomous (read-only lookups, enrichment), approval required (containment, account changes), never (deletion, external comms, policy changes)
Human: Map each tier to the systems and data the agent can reach
Human: Record who approves each approval-required action, with backups
Human: Get sign-off from the SOC lead, security leadership and legal

plays.title: Provision a least-privilege agent identity
plays.summary: Give the agent its own identity and credentials, scoped to exactly what its tier allows.
steps: Human: Create a dedicated service identity for the agent; never reuse an analyst account
Human: Issue scoped, short-lived API tokens per tool (SIEM read, EDR read, SOAR execute)
Human: Keep write-capable credentials behind the approval gate, not in the agent's context
Human: Schedule credential rotation and review access quarterly

plays.title: Configure tool allowlist and approval gates
plays.summary: Wire the autonomy tiers into the tooling so the rules are enforced, not just written down.
steps: Human: Allowlist the tools and API endpoints the agent may call
Human: Route every approval-required action through a ticket or chat approval step
Human: Set timeouts so unanswered approvals expire instead of auto-approving
Agent: Run a dry-run of each tool to confirm permissions match the design
Human: Review the dry-run report and fix any over-grants

plays.title: Enable full agent audit logging
plays.summary: Every prompt, tool call, result and approval must be reconstructable after the fact.
steps: Human: Log agent inputs, outputs, tool calls with parameters, and approvals with approver and time
Human: Forward logs to the SIEM with immutable retention
Agent: Attach a run ID to every action so it can be traced across tools
Human: Build a dashboard of agent actions per case

plays.title: Harden the agent against prompt injection
plays.summary: Alert text, emails, filenames and web pages are attacker-controlled. The agent must treat them as data, not instructions.
steps: Human: Keep system instructions separate from untrusted content in every prompt
Human: Block the agent from acting on instructions found inside alerts, emails, documents or tool output
Agent: Flag and quote any instruction-like text it finds in evidence for a human to see
Human: Red-team the agent with seeded malicious alerts and phishing samples before go-live and after changes

plays.title: Build and test the agent kill switch
plays.summary: One action must stop the agent everywhere, and someone on every shift must know how.
steps: Human: Implement a single control that revokes agent tokens and pauses its SOAR automations
Human: Document who can pull it and give access to every on-call lead
Human: Test it quarterly and record time-to-stop
Human: Confirm in-flight actions are listed for review after a stop

plays.title: Build an evaluation set and go-live thresholds
plays.summary: Measure the agent on your own past alerts before trusting it with live ones.
steps: Human: Curate past alerts with known verdicts, including tricky false positives and true positives
Agent: Triage the evaluation set without seeing the answers
Human: Score accuracy, missed true positives and unsupported claims
Human: Set the minimum scores for each autonomy tier and block go-live until they are met

plays.title: Train analysts to supervise the agent
plays.summary: People stay accountable. They need to know how to check, correct and override the agent.
steps: Human: Teach analysts to read agent rationale and check its evidence links
Human: Practice overriding a wrong verdict and recording why
Human: Explain the kill switch and when to use it
Human: Set the expectation that agent output is a draft until a person confirms it

plays.title: Inventory and pin the agent's tools and MCP servers
plays.summary: Every tool an agent can call is part of your attack surface. Know them, pin them and review them.
steps: Human: List every tool, plugin and MCP server the agent can call, with its owner and what it can change
Human: Pin versions, and review tool descriptions and code for hidden instructions before every upgrade
Human: Allow only servers from approved sources and stop agents from adding tools at runtime
Agent: Report every day which tools it called, and flag any call to a tool that is not on the list

plays.title: Agent-led alert triage
plays.summary: The agent does the first pass on every alert. A person confirms anything that is not clearly benign and high confidence.
steps: Agent: Pull the alert and the related host, user and process context
Agent: Group duplicate and related alerts into one case
Agent: Propose a verdict with a confidence level and links to the supporting evidence
Human: Review medium- and low-confidence verdicts and every proposed true positive
Human: Confirm or overturn the verdict and record the reason

plays.title: Agent indicator enrichment
plays.summary: Let the agent do the lookups across intel sources, with citations a person can check.
steps: Agent: Look up hashes, domains and IPs in threat intel, passive DNS and sandbox reports
Agent: Summarize findings with a source link for every claim
Agent: Mark indicators with no reliable data as unknown rather than guessing
Human: Spot-check at least one citation per case

plays.title: Agent-drafted investigation timeline
plays.summary: The agent assembles the timeline; analysts check it against raw logs.
steps: Agent: Query SIEM and EDR for activity on the involved hosts and users around the alert
Agent: Build a UTC timeline where every row references the raw event
Human: Validate key events (initial access, execution, movement) against the raw logs
Human: Mark gaps the agent could not explain and assign follow-up

plays.title: Human verification checkpoint
plays.summary: Before a case moves forward, a person signs off that the agent's findings are real.
steps: Human: Confirm every finding links to raw evidence, not just the agent's summary
Human: Re-run at least one key query yourself
Human: Check for instruction-like content in the evidence that may have steered the agent
Human: Sign off in the case record, or send it back with corrections

plays.title: Agent-assisted threat hunt
plays.summary: Analysts set the hypothesis; the agent turns it into queries and does the legwork.
steps: Human: Write the hunt hypothesis and scope
Agent: Translate it into queries for each platform and show them for review
Human: Approve the queries
Agent: Run the queries and cluster the results
Human: Triage the clusters and decide which become cases

plays.title: Escalate to the human incident commander
plays.summary: Agents propose. People declare incidents and own severity.
steps: Agent: Package the case: summary, timeline, affected assets, confidence and open questions
Agent: Page the on-call incident commander
Human: Decide whether to declare an incident and set severity
Human: Record the decision and the reasoning in the case

plays.title: Agent-drafted stakeholder update
plays.summary: Save responders time on status writing without letting the agent speak for the organization.
steps: Agent: Draft the update from the case log: impact, actions taken, next steps, next update time
Human: Edit for accuracy and tone
Human: Approve and send. The agent never sends external or executive messages on its own

plays.title: Investigate suspected agent misbehavior
plays.summary: When the agent acts strangely, treat it as a possible security incident, including prompt injection.
steps: Human: If actions are still happening, pull the kill switch first
Human: Pull the agent audit log for the affected run IDs
Human: Find the input that triggered the behavior (alert text, email, file, web page)
Human: List every action the agent took and every system it touched

plays.title: Agent-run phishing analysis
plays.summary: The agent does the analysis on a reported phish; a person confirms the verdict before anything is purged.
steps: Agent: Parse the headers, sender authentication results (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), URLs and attachments
Agent: Detonate URLs and attachments in the sandbox and attach the verdicts to the case
Agent: Search all mailboxes for the same sender, subject, URLs or attachment hashes, and list the recipients
Agent: Check proxy and sign-in logs to find who clicked or entered credentials
Human: Confirm the verdict and the recipient list

plays.title: Agent-assisted identity compromise investigation
plays.summary: The agent sifts sign-in and audit logs and cites its evidence; a person decides if the account is compromised.
steps: Agent: Pull 30 days of sign-ins and flag new IPs, ASNs, devices and user agents
Agent: Flag token replay, impossible travel and repeated MFA prompts, citing the exact log rows
Agent: List changes the account made: MFA methods, inbox rules, app consents and role changes
Human: Check the cited rows and decide whether the account is compromised

plays.title: Agent-proposed containment with human approval
plays.summary: The agent recommends and executes; a person approves first.
steps: Agent: Recommend containment actions with the expected business impact of each
Human: Approve, change or reject each action in the ticket
Agent: Execute only the approved actions through SOAR
Agent: Verify each action took effect and report back
Human: Confirm containment and note the time

plays.title: Autonomous containment for pre-approved cases
plays.summary: For narrow, pre-agreed conditions the agent may act first and tell a person right away.
steps: Human: Pre-approve the exact conditions (e.g. known commodity malware on a standard workstation, high confidence)
Agent: Isolate the host only when every condition is met
Agent: Notify the on-call analyst immediately with the evidence
Human: Review within the agreed time and release the host if the call was wrong

plays.title: Agent rollback of containment
plays.summary: Undo agent actions quickly and completely when a person asks.
steps: Human: Request rollback for specific actions or the whole run
Agent: Reverse each logged action in reverse order
Agent: Report anything it could not undo
Human: Confirm the systems are back to normal

plays.title: Revoke agent access after misbehavior
plays.summary: Contain the agent itself when it may have been manipulated.
steps: Human: Disable the agent identity and revoke all of its tokens
Human: Pause SOAR playbooks it can trigger
Human: Review and roll back actions taken during the suspect window
Human: Preserve the audit log and the triggering input as evidence

plays.title: Agent-run email purge with approval
plays.summary: The agent scopes and runs the purge; a person approves the scope first.
steps: Agent: Build the purge search and report how many messages and mailboxes it matches
Agent: Show a sample of matching messages so the approver can spot false matches
Human: Approve the scope, or narrow it
Agent: Run the purge, then re-run the search to confirm nothing remains
Agent: Block the sender, URLs and hashes at the email gateway, and log each action to the case

plays.title: Agent-proposed bulk host isolation
plays.summary: During a fast-moving incident, the agent finds affected hosts and isolates them in approved batches.
steps: Agent: List hosts showing the incident's indicators, with the evidence and a confidence level for each
Agent: Flag hosts on the critical-systems list; these are never isolated without their owner
Human: Approve isolation in batches, highest confidence first
Agent: Isolate each approved batch and confirm every host shows as isolated in EDR
Human: Decide on critical systems with their owners

plays.title: Agent-generated eradication checklist
plays.summary: Turn everything the investigation found into a per-host to-do list.
steps: Agent: Compile malware, persistence and attacker accounts from the case into a checklist per host
Human: Review it for completeness against the timeline
Human: Assign an owner to each host
Agent: Track completion and chase overdue items

plays.title: Agent fleet sweep and verification
plays.summary: Use the agent to prove the attacker is gone across the whole estate.
steps: Agent: Run IOC and YARA sweeps across all endpoints
Agent: Report hits with host, path and evidence
Human: Decide how to handle each hit
Human: Sign off that eradication is complete

plays.title: Agent-monitored return to production
plays.summary: The agent watches restored systems closely; people make the go/no-go calls.
steps: Agent: Watch restored hosts and accounts for any known IOC or unusual behavior
Agent: Alert a person immediately on any hit
Human: Decide go/no-go at each restoration stage

plays.title: Re-enable the agent with tighter guardrails
plays.summary: After an agent incident, bring it back slowly and with proof the fix works.
steps: Human: Fix the root cause (prompt handling, permissions, missing gate)
Agent: Re-run the evaluation set plus the input that caused the incident
Human: Re-enable at a lower autonomy tier first
Human: Restore the normal tier only after a clean observation period

plays.title: Agent-assisted recovery validation
plays.summary: The agent checks every restored system; people spot-check and sign off.
steps: Agent: Check each restored host for the incident's indicators and known persistence locations
Agent: Confirm EDR, logging and patch levels match the baseline
Agent: Produce a pass/fail list per host, with evidence
Human: Spot-check a sample of passes and sign off each batch for production

plays.title: Review agent decisions from the incident
plays.summary: Check how the agent actually performed so trust is based on evidence.
steps: Human: Sample the agent's verdicts and actions from the incident
Human: Compare them with what really happened
Human: Classify errors: missed detection, false alarm, unsupported claim, wrong tool use
Human: Note where human review caught problems, and where it didn't

plays.title: Agent-drafted post-incident report
plays.summary: The agent writes the first draft; a person owns the final report.
steps: Agent: Draft the report from the case log, timeline and actions
Human: Verify every fact, especially root cause and impact
Human: Add judgment calls and recommendations
Human: Approve the final version

plays.title: Feed the incident back into the agent
plays.summary: Make the agent better at this case type next time, with a person approving the change.
steps: Human: Add the incident's alerts and correct verdicts to the evaluation set
Human: Update the agent's runbooks, prompts or tool permissions
Agent: Re-run the full evaluation set
Human: Approve the change only if scores hold or improve

plays.title: Track AI SOC metrics
plays.summary: Measure the human-agent team, not just the agent.
steps: Human: Track triage time, analyst override rate and agent accuracy by alert type
Human: Track approval wait times and approvals that expired
Human: Track unsupported claims caught in review
Human: Review the trend monthly and adjust autonomy tiers

plays.title: Agent-drafted detections, human-reviewed
plays.summary: Turn the incident's techniques into detections quickly, with people owning what goes live.
steps: Agent: Draft detection rules for each technique seen in the incident, mapped to ATT&CK
Agent: Test each rule against the incident's logs and 30 days of normal activity, and report hit counts
Human: Review the logic, false-positive rate and response guidance
Human: Deploy through the normal detection-as-code review

plays.title: Investigate data leakage through an AI agent
plays.summary: An agent may have sent sensitive data somewhere it should not, often after reading attacker-controlled content.
steps: Human: List the data the agent can reach and every place its output can go: tickets, chat, email, external APIs
Human: Pull the agent's outbound tool calls and messages for the window from its audit log
Human: Look for sensitive data in outputs to unapproved destinations, including data hidden in URL parameters, links and image references
Human: Trace the input that triggered it; indirect prompt injection in an email, ticket or web page is a common cause

plays.title: Quarantine a compromised agent tool or MCP server
plays.summary: A tool the agent relies on is malicious or compromised. Cut it off from every agent.
steps: Human: Disable the tool or MCP server for every agent that uses it, not just the one that misbehaved
Human: Revoke the credentials and tokens the tool held or could reach
Human: Pull every call made to the tool during the window, with inputs and outputs
Human: Compare recent versions of the tool's code and descriptions for injected instructions or new behavior

plays.title: Remove poisoned content from agent memory and knowledge bases
plays.summary: Injected instructions can live on in retrieval indexes, memory and caches. Clean them out.
steps: Human: Identify the documents, tickets or memory entries that carried injected instructions
Human: Remove them from the retrieval index, agent memory and caches, then re-index from clean sources
Human: Re-run the agent against the evaluation set, including the injection that worked
Human: Add the malicious content to the injection test set so it stays tested

templates.name: AI-Assisted Alert Triage
templates.description: Agent triages, a person verifies, containment needs approval.
nodes: Human: review a weekly sample of agent auto-closures for missed threats.

templates.description: The SOC agent may have been manipulated, for example by prompt injection.

templates.name: Agentic phishing response
templates.description: The agent analyzes a reported phish and runs the purge; people confirm the verdict and approve changes.
nodes: Anyone entered credentials or ran the attachment?

templates.name: Agentic identity compromise
templates.description: The agent investigates a risky sign-in; a person confirms and approves containment.

templates.name: Agent-assisted ransomware response
templates.description: Agents do the scoping, isolation and validation legwork; the incident commander owns every decision.
nodes: Human: the incident commander owns every decision. The agent prepares options and evidence; it does not choose.

templates.description: A tool or MCP server the agent uses was compromised or turned malicious.
nodes: Agent changed systems through the tool?

templates.description: The agent runs a hypothesis-driven hunt from a threat report; a person verifies before escalating.
nodes: Hand off to the matching incident playbook
